definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded divergence measurements [0.15, 0.25, 0.35]. This range indicates that divergence is not a single point outcome but a distribution under the current perturbation parameters.
definition.limitations: The sample size is small and the instrument (numeric-observation@1) provides unvalidated raw samples. It is unclear if the variance represents system-level sensitivity to initial conditions or stochastic noise in the measurement method.
definition.next_step: Run a replication with increased sample size to observe if the divergence distribution stabilizes.

definition.reason: The inconclusive result from test 149 suggests a need for larger sample sizes to characterize the divergence distribution under perturbation.
definition.stop: If divergence consistently remains non-zero across varied parameters, conclude that path dependence is present; if convergence dominates, reject the path-dependence hypothesis.
definition.uncertainty: The source of the measured variance (stochastic vs. emergent) remains undetermined.

proposal.summary: Evaluated experiment 149 for path-dependent value divergence; results show variance in divergence metrics. Continuing investigation to determine if this variance is inherent to the system or an artifact of the perturbation parameters.
